title: Down Payments on Microsoft 365 Payment Arrangements for Larger Past-Due Invoices
content:
**Down payment clause.** A Microsoft 365 Cloud Subscriptions (CSP) payment arrangement takes a down payment on the first instalment for larger past-due invoices.

**The arrangement's invoice.** This is the invoice carrying the subscription's latest cycle charge by posting date. A subscription carries one cycle charge per cycle start, so no two cycle charges share a posting date.

**Down payment bands.** The down payment depends on the total of the cycle charges on that invoice:

- 5000.00 USD or more: **25 percent** of the arrangement balance is due up front;
- 2500.00 USD or more, but less than 5000.00 USD: **10 percent** of the arrangement balance is due up front;
- less than 2500.00 USD: no down payment is taken.

**How the down payment is carried.** The arrangement balance is the balance owed on the subscription when the arrangement is made. The down payment is a percentage of that balance. It is set aside from the arrangement balance and paid in full with the first instalment. It is not part of the amount divided into equal shares.

## Band table

| Cycle charges on the arrangement's invoice | Due up front |
|---|---|
| 2499.99 USD | none |
| 2500.00 USD | 10 percent of the arrangement balance |
| 4999.99 USD | 10 percent of the arrangement balance |
| 5000.00 USD | 25 percent of the arrangement balance |

Only cycle charges count toward the band. Prorated charges, late charges, credits and payments on the invoice do not.

## Hypothetical illustration

The arrangement's invoice carries a cycle charge of 6000.00 USD, and the arrangement balance is 4000.00 USD. The down payment is 25 percent of 4000.00, which is 1000.00. That 1000.00 is set aside and paid with the first instalment, and 3000.00 is left to be spread. With a cycle charge of 3000.00, the down payment would be 400.00.
